pencereler.0-5: Part of the core at Three Mile Island melted down. Cooling water escaped for
pencereler.5-12: hours through a valve stuck open. The operators didn't know. Their panel light said the valve was closed. It
pencereler.12-20: only showed the close signal was sent, not the valve's position. Thinking there was too much water, they cut emergency cooling. The
pencereler.20-30: core overheated and partly melted. That's why control rooms and training were rebuilt afterward.

segmentler.metin: Three Mile Island Unit 2 partially melted down.
It took only a relief valve stuck open while its light said closed.
So how could a relief valve stuck open while its light said closed do this?
The answer is loss of coolant through a stuck-open pilot-operated relief valve, misread by operators — and it is why control rooms were redesigned and operator training was overhauled.
